children: Potentially sensitive components from an Australian F-35 fighter jet were mistakenly routed to Hong Kong and subsequently taken into Chinese government custody, raising concerns about the security of the stealth aircraft’s global supply chain.

UPS was transporting a cockpit canopy and weapons-bay door from Australia to the U.S. in late May for inspection and possible repair or disposal, Bloomberg News reported Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The Lockheed Martin
components were coated with radar-absorbing material used to reduce the F-35’s radar signature.

The shipment stopped in South Korea before being diverted to Hong Kong for reasons that remain unclear. Chinese authorities later took possession of the components and haven’t returned them, according to the report.
The incident presents a potential security and oversight problem for Lockheed

and the Pentagon’s sprawling F-35 program. While there’s no indication the episode will materially affect Lockheed’s financial results, it could lead to tighter shipping and supply-chain controls, particularly for sensitive components moving among the roughly 20 countries operating the aircraft. The episode also comes as the U.S. considers additional F-35 sales to countries where technology-security concerns have previously complicated negotiations.

The Pentagon said it’s working with U.S. authorities and industry partners to recover the components and investigate how the shipment was diverted. Officials also are considering safeguards intended to prevent similar incidents.

At least two congressional committees, House Armed Services and House Foreign Affairs, are examining the incident. Pentagon officials also discussed the matter during a closed Senate Armed Services Committee F-35 hearing in June.
reported the diversion to the State Department office responsible for enforcing defense export controls. Australia is separately reviewing its role in the shipment.

Lockheed said transportation requirements were established by the Defense Department and that it selected a carrier consistent with those requirements. The company said it’s working with the carrier on additional oversight measures.

The F-35 is Lockheed’s largest defense program and is operated by the U.S. and numerous allied countries. Australia serves as an Indo-Pacific hub for F-35 parts and maintenance, making the handling of components across international borders an important part of the program’s logistics network.

title: F-35 parts with stealth coating diverted to Hong Kong, taken by China
